title: 100 days / 500 Codeforces problems
goal: Strong independent coverage through 1800; selected transfer through 2000. No universal-solve or rating guarantee.
interface: Cursor for code; Codex for teaching/review; PDF for handwriting

dailyAllocation.activity: Cold recall / revisit one previous idea
Small lesson with one worked example
Five mixed problem slots; distribute time freely
Review the most useful miss and save available evidence

families.name: Prefix sums, differences and two pointers
Number theory, combinatorics, bits and elementary geometry
Graph traversal, DSU and shortest paths
Rooted trees, tree DP and ancestor queries
Range data structures and offline queries

lessons: Read the objective; inspect a tiny case
Compare two approaches; find a counterexample
Graph/tree and DP micro-diagnostic; repair one prerequisite
Review the first five days; choose three priorities
Two pointers: why can a pointer move?
Windows: what is the maintained quantity?
First true: write the predicate and boundary
Greedy exchange argument; compare with graph modeling

weeks.focus: DP state design and binary reasoning
lessons: Define a state in one complete sentence
Binary place values and bit operators
XOR cancellation; masks as small sets
Root, parent, children, depth and traversal order
Sieve, prime factors and exponent counts
Connect a tree invariant to an array invariant

weeks.focus: DP choices and search on answers
lessons: Exchange proof or recurrence: choose from evidence
DSU representative and union by size
0-1 BFS and when ordinary BFS fails
Fenwick prefix query and point update
Offline queries: sort events and state the order
Choose a root and identify changing quantities
Binary lifting and lowest common ancestor
Tree queries with earlier range tools
Prefix function: border meaning and fallback
Iterative segment tree: combine and identity
Range update and lazy propagation on a small trace
Monotonic stack/deque: what can be discarded?
DAG DP: process only settled predecessors
Interval DP: state and split point
SCCs and condensation: teach before an application
Bridges: entry time and low-link meaning
Digit DP: tight/started state, only if earlier DP holds
Elementary geometry: orientation and integer predicates

weeks.focus: Constructive thinking and small state spaces
lessons: Subset enumeration and bounded bitmask DP
Meet in the middle when full enumeration is too large
Small games: terminal states and winning/losing states
Contrasting problems with deceptively similar stories
Cold retrieval of a previously assisted idea
Explain why a tempting alternative fails
One reachable stretch; consolidate the rest
Range or graph composition, subject to readiness
Revisit an assisted idea without its old code
Mixed transfer; replace any untaught specialty
Review and choose the final evidence sample

weeks.focus: Final transfer audit and next steps
lessons: Unseen mixed sample; preserve help history
Unseen mixed sample; inspect proof quality
Unseen mixed sample; check Python constraints
Finish the audit; summarize strengths and remaining gaps

selectionPolicy.futureAssignments: Provisional named candidates, not 495 independently audited solution paths. Recheck the official statement/editorial, prerequisites, Python feasibility and exposure before releasing each day. Preserve slot count and history on substitution.
selectionPolicy.topicLabels: Coach-only; learner daily cards and PDF rows omit family, tags and rating. This is separation of views, not a security boundary.
selectionPolicy.distinctness: 500 distinct IDs and names; excludes 305 prior accepted IDs and inspected prior exposure except explicit 1690D repair. A later re-solve does not add to the 500.
selectionPolicy.counting: A new AC is accepted evidence. Meaningful completion additionally requires learner implementation and an explicit coach reasoning review; independence requires the learner to confirm no hints/editorial/AI solution.
selectionPolicy.adaptation: Use Sunday evidence; preserve 180 minutes, at most three priorities; revise unopened candidates instead of manufacturing success.
